questions.prompt: A source shows a first-year request of 178,000 and a full project request of 485,000. The field requires the full project request. Three runs return 178,000, and the consistency measure is high. What does that evidence support?

choices.text: Accept the amount because repeated agreement establishes accuracy.
choices.feedback: The repeated value answers the wrong period. Agreement does not make it accurate.

choices.text: Treat it as a repeatable error and repair the field interpretation before using the total.
choices.feedback: The source and field definition establish a mismatch even though the runs agree.

choices.text: Average the two source amounts to produce a safer total.
choices.feedback: Averaging distinct annual and full-period values invents an unsupported answer.

questions.prompt: A template has a high quality score from three clean, short documents tested last month. Today you use a longer document with an unfamiliar layout, and the deadline has no visible source support. What is justified?

choices.text: Treat the current deadline as certified because the template has a high score.
choices.feedback: The historical measurement does not establish an unsupported value in a different input.

choices.text: Discard every earlier measurement as useless because it is historical.
choices.feedback: Earlier measurements still describe their tested conditions; assess their relevance and limits.

choices.text: Keep the deadline unresolved, inspect its source and test relevant cases for the new input type.
choices.feedback: Use the score within its measured scope and obtain evidence for the current value and input type.

questions.prompt: You saved a repair to an extraction prompt. Workflow validation then reports a passing result, but its execution record predates the edit. Which claim can you make?

choices.text: The new prompt passed because validation was run after the edit.
choices.feedback: The evaluation time does not change which execution produced the assessed output.

choices.text: The older execution passed those checks; execute the saved repair and evaluate its actual result.
choices.feedback: The new behavior needs a new linked execution. Preserve the older result as historical evidence.

choices.text: The assistant says the repair is sound, so a new run is unnecessary.
choices.feedback: A predicted improvement does not establish the changed workflow's result.

questions.prompt: You finalize a guided verification session after approving four fields and skipping an uncertain project-period field. Later validation is strong on the saved expected values. What does that establish?

choices.text: Every original field, including project period, was checked successfully.
choices.feedback: The skipped field was omitted from expected values, so the score cannot establish its accuracy.

choices.text: The included expectations were measured; the skipped field still needs source-checked coverage.
choices.feedback: Finalization saves approved/corrected expectations. Skipped fields remain a coverage limitation.

choices.text: Project period has become optional for every future task.
choices.feedback: Skipping one unconfirmed expectation does not redefine the workflow or course requirements.
